subject.title: [Feature]: Support configurable request labels for Gemini API calls (GCP billing tracking)

question: Should OpenClaw expose static request labels for Google Vertex generateContent calls, and what public config shape and validation/privacy limits should own that contract?
rationale: The request adds a provider billing-metadata contract with compatibility, privacy, and cardinality implications; current code has possible existing config surfaces but no approved label semantics.

options.title: Approve Vertex-only static labels
options.body: Add a Google-plugin-owned Vertex label contract, preferably through the maintainer-approved existing params/config path, with strict label validation, low-cardinality guidance, docs, tests, and live proof.

options.title: Design cross-provider attribution first
options.body: Keep this open while maintainers decide whether billing attribution should become a broader provider metadata concept instead of a Google-specific key.

options.title: Decline in-product labels
options.body: Tell operators to handle billing attribution outside OpenClaw, accepting that shared GCP projects remain hard to attribute from OpenClaw alone.

recommendation.title: Approve Vertex-only static labels
recommendation.body: Add a Google-plugin-owned Vertex label contract, preferably through the maintainer-approved existing params/config path, with strict label validation, low-cardinality guidance, docs, tests, and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current-history signal for the Google provider transport and config surfaces where this product/config decision would land.
